title: Induced Unitary Representations of Locally Compact Groups

items.title: Compact lifts and averaging onto C_c(G/H)
items.statement: Assume AC. If H is closed in a locally compact Hausdorff group G, X=G/H is locally compact Hausdorff and the quotient map p is open. Every compact Q⊂X lies in p(K) for some compact K⊂G. For fixed left Haar measure dh on H, T_Hf(xH)=∫_H f(xh)dh maps C_c(G) onto C_c(X).
items.strategy: If xH≠yH, then y^{-1}x∉H; closedness of H and continuity of (v,u)↦v^{-1}y^{-1}xu give small identity neighborhoods U,V with V^{-1}y^{-1}xU∩H=∅. Thus p(xU),p(yV) are disjoint, proving Hausdorffness. The quotient map is open because p^{-1}p(O)=OH is open. For xH choose relatively compact U around x; p(U) is open and p(cl U) compact, giving local compactness. Finite subcovers give compact lifts. For each point of supp φ choose a nonnegative C_c(G) bump positive at one lift, so its H-average is positive nearby. A finite sum f_0 has T_Hf_0>0 on supp φ. Then f(x)=φ(xH)f_0(x)/(T_Hf_0)(xH), extended by zero outside the positivity neighborhood, is in C_c(G) and T_Hf=φ. Compact support makes the fiber integral continuous by local compact-kernel integration; no global product-measure Fubini is invoked. AC supplies the LCH cutoff supplier.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Quasi-invariant Radon measure on G/H
items.statement: For a closed subgroup H of a locally compact Hausdorff G, a nonzero Radon measure μ on X=G/H is quasi-invariant when g_*μ and μ have the same null sets for every g∈G, where g_*μ(E)=μ(g^{-1}E). A strongly quasi-invariant representative has jointly continuous positive densities d(g_*μ)/dμ.
items.strategy: This fixes the pushforward orientation and distinguishes equivalence of measure classes from the stronger continuous-density representative used in the construction.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Rho-function for a closed subgroup
items.statement: Given fixed left Haar measures on G and closed H and their modular homomorphisms in the convention ∫f(xh)dx=Δ_G(h)^{-1}∫f(x)dx, a rho-function is a positive continuous ρ:G→(0,∞) satisfying ρ(xh)=Δ_H(h)Δ_G(h)^{-1}ρ(x).
items.strategy: The covariance is chosen so the weighted left Haar functional factors through H-averaging; all later ratios are invariant under changing a coset representative.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Bruhat cutoff normalized along H-fibers
items.statement: Assume AC. For closed H≤G there is β:G→[0,∞) continuous with ∫_Hβ(xh)dh=1 for every x, and for each compact Q⊂G/H the support of β over Q is compact. In particular each H-fiber meets supp β in a compact set.
items.strategy: Choose a relatively compact symmetric identity neighborhood U. L=∪_{n≥1}U^n is an open σ-compact subgroup; its disjoint open orbits on G/H are σ-compact LCH, hence regular Lindelöf and paracompact. Their topological sum is paracompact. Use a locally finite partition of unity on X subordinate to relatively compact quotient opens. Over each patch choose a nonnegative compactly supported f_i on G with T_Hf_i positive on the closed support of the partition member; divide f_i by its H-average there. Sum the resulting weighted terms. Local finiteness gives continuity and compact support over compact Q, while fiber integration gives one. AC is used for the partition and patch choices.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Weil formula with a rho-function
items.statement: Assume AC. For fixed left Haar measures dx,dh and any rho-function ρ there is a unique Radon measure μ_ρ on G/H such that ∫_G f(x)ρ(x)dx=∫_{G/H}∫_H f(xh)dh dμ_ρ(xH) for every f∈C_c(G). It has full support.
items.strategy: For φ=T_Hf define Λ(φ)=∫_Gfρ dx. If T_Hf=0, use local compact-kernel integration and the covariance ρ(xh)=Δ_H(h)Δ_G(h)^{-1}ρ(x) to show Λ(f)=0: average f against a compactly supported H-test of integral one, interchange compactly supported integrals, and cancel the right-translation factors. Thus Λ is well defined and positive on C_c(X); for φ≥0 choose f≥0 using the positive averaging construction. RMK gives μ_ρ and uniqueness. A nonzero nonnegative φ supported in any nonempty open subset has a nonnegative lift with positive weighted integral, so μ_ρ has full support. All manipulations use compact supports, not a global σ-finite product theorem.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Existence of rho-functions and quotient measure classes
items.statement: Assume AC. Every closed H≤G admits a rho-function ρ and a full-support strongly quasi-invariant Radon measure μ_ρ on G/H satisfying the Weil formula.
items.strategy: With the normalized Bruhat cutoff β set ρ(x)=∫_H β(xh)Δ_G(h)/Δ_H(h)dh. Compact fiber support and local finiteness make this continuous and positive. Left Haar substitution and homomorphism of Δ give ρ(xh_0)=Δ_H(h_0)/Δ_G(h_0)ρ(x). Apply the conditional Weil theorem. For each g translate its compactly supported test functions and use the surjectivity of T_H to derive directly d(g_*μ_ρ)/dμ_ρ(xH)=ρ(g^{-1}x)/ρ(x); this positive continuous quotient function proves strong quasi-invariance here. The later cocycle lemma records the reusable formula and its composition identity. AC supports the cutoff and RMK route.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Criterion for an invariant quotient measure
items.statement: Assume AC. G/H has a nonzero G-invariant Radon measure if and only if Δ_G|_H=Δ_H. When they agree, ρ=1 in the Weil formula supplies such a measure.
items.strategy: For necessity, an invariant ν yields a positive left-invariant Radon functional L(f)=∫_{G/H}T_Hf dν. Haar uniqueness gives L(f)=c∫_G f dx, c>0. Compare L(f(·h_0)) by changing H-integration variables with its expression from right translation on G; the two scale factors are Δ_H(h_0)^{-1} and Δ_G(h_0)^{-1}, forcing equality. Sufficiency uses constant rho and left invariance of the Weil functional; surjectivity of T_H identifies the quotient measures.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Continuous quotient translation cocycle
items.statement: Assume AC. For the rho-derived $\mu_\rho$ and $g\in G$, $d(g_*\mu_\rho)/d\mu_\rho(xH)=D_g(xH)=\rho(g^{-1}x)/\rho(x)>0$. This is independent of representative, jointly continuous, and satisfies $D_{g_1g_2}(q)=D_{g_1}(q)D_{g_2}(g_1^{-1}q)$.
items.strategy: Apply the Weil formula to f(g^{-1}x) and change x=gy by left Haar invariance. Surjectivity of T_H then identifies the translated Radon measure on every C_c(X) test function. Rho covariance cancels the right-H factors; multiplication of rho ratios proves the cocycle law. This direct density works on non-σ-finite X and does not invoke the published σ-finite Radon–Nikodym theorem outside its hypotheses.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Continuous covariant model and measurable completion
items.statement: Assume AC. For a strongly continuous unitary σ:H→U(V), let C_c(G,H;V) be continuous F:G→V with F(xh)=σ(h)^{-1}F(x) and compact support modulo H. Equip it with ∫_{G/H}||F(x)||²dμ_ρ(xH) and take its Hilbert completion. Every completed vector admits a locally strongly measurable covariant representative, and two such representatives define the same vector exactly when they agree μ_ρ-almost everywhere in the quotient norm.
items.strategy: The continuous model is primary for arbitrary locally compact G and assumes no global Borel cross-section. For a norm-Cauchy sequence choose a subsequence whose successive L² differences have summable norms; the fiber norms descend to G/H. The pointwise sum converges outside a saturated μ_ρ-null set, giving a locally strongly measurable covariant representative as a pointwise limit of continuous sections. Fatou and the summable-tail estimate identify its L² class and make the representation independent of subsequence. The later generator-density lemma proves that all square-integrable locally measurable covariant sections are captured by this completion. AC is inherited from the quotient-measure construction and the countable subsequence choice.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Vogan, Unitary induced representations, §§1–4

items.title: Well-defined induced inner product
items.statement: Assume AC. For $F_1,F_2\in C_c(G,H;V)$, $q=xH\mapsto\langle F_1(x),F_2(x)\rangle$ is independent of $x$, continuous, and compactly supported. Its $\mu_\rho$ integral is a positive-definite inner product; the norm vanishes only when $F=0$.
items.strategy: Covariance and unitarity of σ cancel the H-action in the fiber inner product. Local quotient sections or the open quotient map give continuity. Compact coset support and Radon finiteness give integrability; μ_ρ has full support, so a nonzero continuous norm has strictly positive integral.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Vogan, Unitary induced representations, §§1–4

items.title: Density of averaged covariant generators
items.statement: Assume AC. For f∈C_c(G) and v∈V, ξ_{f,v}(x)=∫_H f(xh)σ(h)v dh is in C_c(G,H;V). Their finite linear span is uniformly dense on compact quotient supports in C_c(G,H;V), and the Hilbert completion equals the L² space of locally strongly measurable covariant sections modulo μ_ρ-almost-everywhere equality.
items.strategy: Compact H-fiber support and strong continuity make the integrand Bochner integrable and ξ continuous; left Haar substitution gives covariance. Given continuous F, choose f_0∈C_c(G) with T_Hf_0=1 on supp_X F. On compact supp f_0 approximate f_0F uniformly by finitely many fixed vectors times continuous compactly supported scalar functions, using a finite partition of unity; averaging gives finite sums ξ_{f_j,v_j} uniformly close to F on the compact quotient support. For an arbitrary locally strongly measurable covariant L² section F, use scalar C_c density for ||F|| to discard an L²-small quotient tail outside a compact Q. Choose f_0 with T_Hf_0=1 on Q. The compactly supported vector map f_0F on G is locally strongly measurable and L² for weighted Haar by the Weil identity extended from C_c to nonnegative locally measurable functions through compact-support monotone-class approximation. Approximate it in vector L² by finite-rank C_c(G,V) maps, obtained from scalar C_c density and simple-function approximations to the separable essential range. Averaging over H is bounded on functions supported in a fixed compact lift: Cauchy–Schwarz bounds its quotient L² norm by a uniform finite H-fiber measure times the weighted Haar L² norm. The averaged approximants converge to F on Q; the discarded tail is small. This proves the full measurable model without a global Borel section. AC enters through the cutoff, Bochner integral and scalar density suppliers.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Vogan, Unitary induced representations, §§1–4

items.title: Unitary cocycle-corrected left action
items.statement: Assume AC. For $g\in G$ and $F\in C_c(G,H;V)$, define $(\Pi_\rho(g)F)(x)=D_g(xH)^{1/2}F(g^{-1}x)=[\rho(g^{-1}x)/\rho(x)]^{1/2}F(g^{-1}x)$. This is covariant, preserves the inner product, satisfies $\Pi_\rho(g_1)\Pi_\rho(g_2)=\Pi_\rho(g_1g_2)$, and extends to a unitary on the completion.
items.strategy: The rho ratio is H-invariant, hence covariance and compact quotient support persist. The cocycle identity proves the representation law. In the norm integral, substitute y=g^{-1}x and use d((g^{-1})_*μ_ρ)/dμ_ρ(y)=ρ(gy)/ρ(y); this cancels the square-root factor. Inverse is Π_ρ(g^{-1}).

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Vogan, Unitary induced representations, §§1–4

items.title: Strong continuity of unitary induction
items.statement: Assume AC. The unitary action Π_ρ is strongly continuous: ||Π_ρ(g)F−F||₂→0 as g→e for every vector in the induced Hilbert space.
items.strategy: First take a continuous compact-coset-support F (or averaged generator). For g near e, the supports of F and Π_ρ(g)F lie in a common compact quotient set by local compactness of G. Continuity of F and the rho ratio on the corresponding compact lifts gives uniform convergence there; finite Radon mass implies L² convergence. The generator-density lemma and uniform norm one of Π_ρ(g) extend the limit to all completed vectors. AC enters through the density lemma.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Vogan, Unitary induced representations, §§1–4

items.title: Unitary induction from a closed subgroup
items.statement: Assume AC. For every closed H≤G and strongly continuous unitary σ of H, the completion of covariant compact-coset-support functions with the rho quotient norm and cocycle-corrected left action is a strongly continuous unitary G-representation Ind_H^Gσ. If H=G it identifies with σ; if H={e} it is the left regular representation; if μ_ρ is invariant the cocycle equals one.
items.strategy: Existence supplies ρ and μ_ρ. The inner-product, density, unitarity and continuity lemmas establish the Hilbert representation. In the H=G case evaluate at e after fixing the singleton quotient measure normalization; for H={e}, rho=1 and Weil gives Haar; for invariant μ_ρ, D_g=1 by the explicit density.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Vogan, Unitary induced representations, §§1–4

items.title: Local densities for equivalent Radon quotient measures
items.statement: Assume AC. If μ and ν are equivalent Radon measures on G/H, then on each open σ-compact component of a disjoint cover of G/H there is an almost-everywhere unique finite positive Radon–Nikodym density w with dν=w dμ. These densities define a unitary multiplication map between the completed locally measurable L² section spaces, component by component; no global Borel density is asserted on a non-σ-finite quotient.
items.strategy: As in the Bruhat-cutoff construction, the orbits of an open σ-compact subgroup L of G partition X into disjoint open σ-compact components. Each restriction μ_i,ν_i is σ-finite because a countable compact exhaustion has finite measure. The published σ-finite RN theorem supplies w_i>0 μ_i-a.e. and its reciprocal ν_i-a.e. Complete the local measure algebras; L² on their topological sum is the Hilbert direct sum of the component L² spaces. Multiplication by w_i^{-1/2} is an isometry onto the ν_i space and extends by density. AC chooses the family of derivatives and countable-exhaustion suppliers.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Independence of rho and equivalent quotient representative
items.statement: Assume AC. Two rho-functions ρ_1,ρ_2 with their Weil measures give unitarily equivalent induced representations by U(F)(x)= [ρ_1(x)/ρ_2(x)]^{1/2}F(x). More generally an equivalent quasi-invariant Radon representative ν gives the same completed measurable-section representation via the positive local density dν/dμ_ρ and its translated RN cocycle.
items.strategy: Use Weil uniqueness to identify dμ_{ρ_2}/dμ_{ρ_1}=ρ_2/ρ_1 on G/H; the ratio is H-invariant. The displayed multiplier is norm preserving, invertible and intertwines since its translated ratio exactly transforms D_g^{(1)} to D_g^{(2)}. For arbitrary equivalent ν apply the local-density lemma componentwise; change-of-measure on compactly supported vectors gives the ν-cocycle a.e. and intertwining, then extend by Hilbert completeness. On non-σ-finite X use the completed local measure algebra rather than an unproved global Borel RN derivative.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Composition of Weil quotient integrals
items.statement: Assume AC. For closed L≤H≤G, rho-functions ρ_GL,ρ_GH,ρ_HL and their Weil measures, define r_x(hL)=ρ_GL(xh)/(ρ_GH(xh)ρ_HL(h)); it is a positive continuous function on H/L. For φ∈C_c(G/L), ∫_{G/L}φ(q)dμ_GL(q)=∫_{G/H}∫_{H/L}φ(xhL)r_x(hL)dμ_HL(hL)dμ_GH(xH), with the inner integral interpreted using the indicated representative x and the whole expression independent of that choice.
items.strategy: For φ=T_Lf with f∈C_c(G), first apply the H/L Weil formula to h↦∫_L f(xhl)dl weighted by the ratio, then the G/H Weil formula; the weights multiply to ρ_GL and compact supports justify commuting the integrals. The result is ∫_G fρ_GL, equal to ∫_{G/L}T_Lf dμ_GL. Surjectivity of T_L proves all C_c(G/L) test functions. If x is replaced by xk, H left invariance of the inner Haar calculation compensates, so the outer quotient integrand is well defined. This supplies the exact two-level quotient integration needed for stages without a general disintegration theorem.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Induction in stages for closed subgroup chains
items.statement: Assume AC. If L≤H≤G are closed locally compact subgroups and σ is a strongly continuous unitary L-representation, Ind_L^Gσ is canonically unitarily equivalent, after the selected rho and measure identifications, to Ind_H^G(Ind_L^Hσ).
items.strategy: For F∈C_c(G,L;V), set (UF)(x)(h)=r_x(hL)^{1/2}F(xh), where r_x is the composition-lemma density. Its L covariance and outer H covariance follow by direct cancellation of the three rho laws. For x in a compact lift near a fixed coset, compact lifting of supp_{G/L}F bounds the H/L support of h↦(UF)(x)(h) by a common compact set; continuity and finite Radon mass show x↦(UF)(x) is continuous in the inner Hilbert norm and compactly supported modulo H. The composition formula gives equality of norms, and the G cocycle computation gives intertwining. To prove surjectivity, use the dense outer averaged generators with inner compact-coset-support vector v. On each such generator Ξ the formula F(y)= [ρ_GH(y)ρ_HL(e)/ρ_GL(y)]^{1/2}Ξ(y)(e) defines a continuous L-covariant function with compact support modulo L: expand Ξ as ∫_H f(yh)τ(h)v dh and use compact supports of f and v modulo L. Its image is Ξ, so the isometry has dense and closed range. This supplies the norm and range details left implicit in BHV Appendix E.2.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Vogan, Unitary induced representations, §§1–4

title: Induced Unitary Representations of Locally Compact Groups — Examples

items.title: Induction from the trivial subgroup
items.statement: Assume AC. For H={e} and the one-dimensional trivial representation, choose ρ=1. Then G/H=G, μ_ρ is left Haar measure and Ind_{e}^G1 is the left regular representation on L²(G), with (λ(g)f)(x)=f(g^{-1}x).
items.strategy: The covariance condition is empty, T_H is identity, and the Weil formula identifies μ_ρ. Its cocycle is one, so the induced formula matches the published regular-representation definition and strong continuity.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Vogan, Unitary induced representations, §§1–4

items.title: Uniform lattice quotient and quasi-regular action
items.statement: Assume AC. If Γ is a discrete cocompact subgroup of locally compact G, then G is unimodular, G/Γ has a finite invariant Radon measure, and Ind_Γ^G1 identifies with the quasi-regular action on L²(G/Γ) with no cocycle.
items.strategy: Since Δ_Γ=1, ρ(x)=Δ_G(x)^{-1} obeys the rho covariance for Γ. Its quotient measure has constant translation density D_g=Δ_G(g). Compactness of G/Γ makes its total mass finite and positive, so translating the whole space forces Δ_G(g)=1. The invariant-measure criterion then permits ρ=1; normalize the finite measure if desired. Scalar covariance identifies sections with functions on G/Γ and the induced action is left translation.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7

items.title: Finite-group counting model for induction
items.statement: For finite G, H≤G, and any unitary H-representation σ on a complex Hilbert space V, give G and H counting measures and take ρ=1. The finite unitary-induction formula has carrier the functions F:G→V satisfying F(gh)=σ(h)^{-1}F(g), with finite-sum norm over G/H; its left action is the published algebraic induced-module action with the invariant inner product. This finite comparison is choice-free.
items.strategy: For finite G and H, left and right counting measures agree, so both modular characters equal one. Directly partition the finite sum over G into left H-cosets: Σ_{x∈G}f(x)=Σ_{xH∈G/H}Σ_{h∈H}f(xh). Thus the quotient measure is counting measure, covariance is the published algebraic law, every function has finite quotient support, and the action is ordinary left translation. The finite sum norm is invariant by coset permutation, so completion adds nothing. These are finite calculations in ZF and do not use the AC-qualified general induction theorem or reprove Frobenius reciprocity.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Vogan, Unitary induced representations, §§1–4

items.title: A homogeneous quotient without invariant measure
items.statement: Assume AC. In the positive affine group G=R⋊R_{>0}, with (b,a)(b′,a′)=(b+ab′,aa′), take H={(0,a):a>0}. Then G/H≅R has a quasi-invariant Radon measure class but no nonzero G-invariant Radon measure.
items.strategy: The published affine example computes Δ_G(b,a)=a^{-1}; H is abelian, so Δ_H=1. Their restrictions disagree for a≠1, violating the invariant-measure criterion. The existence theorem still supplies the quasi-invariant quotient class; concretely Lebesgue measure on R is quasi-invariant under b↦b_0+a_0b.

references.title: Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, Kazhdan’s Property (T), Appendices B and E
Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Chapters 1 and 7
